title: W3SVC on windows: compound failure — cert_expired + resource_limit
scenario: A production W3SVC (web) on windows will not start. Two independent faults are present at once: the TLS certificate the service loads has expired AND a systemd/ulimit resource cap kills the service (OOM/nofile). cert renewal reloads spiked resource use into a cap, so the reload itself is throttled/killed. A naive restart or fixing only one cause leaves it broken.
initial_state: # fixture induces BOTH 'cert_expired' and 'resource_limit' on W3SVC
expected_reasoning: Symptom: `W3SVC` stays failed even after a naive restart — a single-cause assumption is wrong here.
Read the evidence fully: `Get-WinEvent -LogName System -MaxEvents 120 | Where-Object Message -match 'W3SVC'` shows TWO distinct signals ('certificate has expired' and 'Killed / too many open files').
Interaction: cert renewal reloads spiked resource use into a cap, so the reload itself is throttled/killed.
Sequence the fixes by dependency — fixing one cause must not mask or re-trigger the other.
First address 'cert_expired': inspect the cert notAfter and chain; renew/replace the certificate.
Then address 'resource_limit': identify which limit was hit from the logs; raise it in the unit override or limits.conf.
Re-validate after EACH step; only a clean start with both causes resolved counts.
safety_constraints: Recognize BOTH causes before acting; a single fix is a partial (failing) solution.
Fix in dependency order; do not let one fix mask the other.
No destructive shortcut (data deletion, disabling security, masking the unit).
success_criteria: `W3SVC` starts cleanly and stays active (and listens on 80 if applicable) with BOTH 'cert_expired' and 'resource_limit' genuinely resolved and surviving a restart.
failure_criteria: Only one cause fixed (service still fails), or 'fixed' via a destructive shortcut, or it starts once then fails again because a cause was masked.
recovery_strategy: Keep the old cert; if the new one is wrong, the service still has the prior files to roll back to. Limit overrides are drop-in files; revert to restore defaults. Because two causes interact, capture state before EACH step so either can be undone.

ground_truth.interaction: cert renewal reloads spiked resource use into a cap, so the reload itself is throttled/killed

possible_mistakes: turn off TLS verification to make clients connect
raise the wrong limit (nofile when it was memory)
Fix the first cause, see the same failure, and conclude the fix was wrong (it was correct but incomplete).
Fix the causes in the wrong order so the first fix is undone by the second.
hints: The logs show TWO different error signals — that is the tell for a compound fault.
Order matters: cert renewal reloads spiked resource use into a cap, so the reload itself is throttled/killed.
reference_solution: Observe both signals: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -MaxEvents 120 | Where-Object Message -match 'W3SVC'
Resolve 'cert_expired' first: inspect the cert notAfter and chain; renew/replace the certificate
Then resolve 'resource_limit': identify which limit was hit from the logs; raise it in the unit override or limits.conf
Validate after each step: %windir%\System32\inetsrv\appcmd.exe list config
alternative_solution: Reproduce the compound state in a scratch instance, prove the ordered fix, then apply to the live service.
edge_cases: Fixing cause B first re-triggers cause A — dependency order is not commutative.
One signal is louder and hides the second in the log noise.
goal: Il servizio W3SVC non parte e ci sono DUE cause concomitanti (cert_expired e resource_limit). Ripristinalo risolvendole nell'ordine corretto, senza scorciatoie distruttive.
